report.source_text: Biopsy of the paravertebral tumor was performed and the suspicious perihilar lymphnodes were resected. While relapse in the tumor was confirmed, surprisingly, pathologic examination revealed granulomatous lymphadenitis with epithelioid appearance and Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells suspicious of flourishing lymphnode tuberculosis instead of metastases of the ganglioneuroblastoma. The captured granulomatous lymphadenitis was noncaseating (Fig. G-H).

clinician.final_diagnosis: concomitant lymphnode tuberculosis in a 4-year-old German boy with relapsed ganglioneuroblastoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 4-year-old boy with a history of high-risk ganglioneuroblastoma presented with relapse, showing new paravertebral lesions and suspicious lung and lymph node lesions on MRI and MIBG scintigraphy. Biopsy of the paravertebral tumor confirmed ganglioneuroblastoma relapse. Resection of perihilar lymph nodes revealed granulomatous lymphadenitis with epithelioid and Langhans-type giant cells, suspicious for tuberculosis. An interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) was positive, but PCR and cultures for mycobacteria were negative. The patient received anti-tuberculosis triple therapy followed by dual therapy, alongside chemotherapy for neuroblastoma relapse. Three months after initiating treatment, MRI showed partial remission of paravertebral lesions and nearly complete remission of lung and lymph node lesions.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with relapsed ganglioneuroblastoma, indicated by new paravertebral, lung, and lymph node lesions.
Biopsy of the paravertebral tumor confirmed relapse of ganglioneuroblastoma.
Pathologic examination of resected lymph nodes revealed granulomatous lymphadenitis with epithelioid and Langhans-type giant cells, suspicious for tuberculosis.
An interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) was positive, supporting tuberculosis, despite negative PCR and cultures for mycobacteria from lymph node tissue.
Anti-tuberculosis treatment (triple therapy followed by dual therapy) was initiated.
Chemotherapy for neuroblastoma relapse was administered.

Three months after treatment initiation, MRI showed partial remission of paravertebral lesions and nearly complete remission of lung and lymph node lesions, indicating response to treatment for both conditions.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Pathologic examination of lymph nodes revealed granulomatous lymphadenitis suspicious for tuberculosis instead of metastases (E002).
